2. The predecessor in interest of the appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 23 of 1967 in the court of Munsif, Sunamgonj for declaration of title and khas possession in respect of the land described in the 3rd schedule to the plaint. 

 3. The facts of the original suit in brief are that the suit land belonged to Basir Shah, the maternal grandfather of the plaintiff No. 2 Basir Shah gifted the suit land to the plaintiff No.2. Thereafter Aftabur Reja took khas possession of the 2nd schedule lands by force and then settled it to one Rajob Ali. After the death of Rajob Ali the land lord again took possession of the said land and settled it to Hurmot Ali. Thereafter Hurmot Ali sold the said land to the plaintiff No.1 by registered deed dated 12th July, 1949. Hurmot Ali had two huts but he did not remove the same. Accordingly the plaintiff No.1 instituted Title Suit No.86 of 1950 for recovery of kkhs possession. The suit was disposed of on compromise and the plaintiff No.1 got possession through Court on 4th November, 1951. The defendants tried to cut bamboos from the said land when the plaintiff No.1 instituted a criminal case against him. The defendants threatened the plaintiffs for dispossession in the middle part of Agrahayan, and thereafter the defendants trespassed into the 3rd schedule land out of the 2nd schedule by dispossessing the plaintiffs. 

 11. This is a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. So, the plain-tiffs are to prove their chain of title and mode of possession and date and time of the alleged dispossession.
